title: Company-wide policies and processes: access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel, templates
author: Jordan Patel
body:
Overview
--------
This document centralizes Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel, and internal templates. It is intended to provide a single reference for employees, managers, and auditors and to ensure consistent, auditable decisions across teams.

Scope
-----
Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and third-party vendors with access to company systems, data, facilities, and purchasing privileges. Certain sections reference more detailed team-level or service-level runbooks; those are linked where appropriate.

Key principles
--------------
- Least privilege: Access is granted based on the minimum privileges required to perform job duties.
- Separation of duties: Approvals and authorizations are distinct from execution where possible.
- Auditability: Changes to systems, access, and vendor contracts must be logged and traceable.
- Data minimization and retention: Collect and store only what is required; adhere to retention schedules.
- Cost-conscious procurement: Favor approved vendors, preferred pricing, and procurement thresholds.

1) Access and permissions
------------------------
Purpose: Standardize onboarding, offboarding, role changes, and privileged access for systems and data.

Account lifecycle
- Onboarding: People-ops triggers account creation after offer acceptance. Hiring manager completes the Access Request Form and selects predefined role profiles (e.g., engineering-readonly, infra-admin, finance-approver).
- Role changes: Managers submit a Role Change Request in the HR portal. Access changes should be applied within 2 business days for non-privileged roles and 24 hours for privilege escalations when approved.
- Offboarding: Termination workflow revokes all cloud console, VPN, application, and SaaS access within 4 hours for involuntary terminations and 24 hours for voluntary departures.

Privileged access controls
- Privileged roles (e.g., infra-admin, KMS-admin, payroll-admin) require manager approval plus an owner_team sponsor. Access is time-bounded by default (maximum 90 days) and requires justification.
- Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is mandatory for all privileged accounts.
- Break-glass process: Requests for emergency elevated access must be logged in the incident tracking system and approved by on-call infra and security leads; all sessions are recorded.

Access review and attestations
- Quarterly access review is owned by team leads; remediation tasks must complete within 10 business days.
- External contractors' access is reviewed monthly.

Table: Typical approval levels
| Action | Requester | Approver | Notes |
| Grant non-privileged access | Manager | System owner | Apply role template |
| Grant privileged access | Manager + owner_team | Security lead | Time-bound, justify |
| Vendor access to production | Vendor manager | Security + infra | Contract in place, NDA; limited IP ranges |

2) Change management
--------------------
Purpose: Ensure predictable, testable, auditable changes to production services and infrastructure.

Change categories
- Standard changes: Routine, pre-authorized (e.g., scheduled certificate renewals). No CAB required but must be documented in change log.
- Minor changes: Low risk, require owner_team approval and automatic scheduling.
- Major changes: Impactful changes (schema migrations, runtime upgrades). Require a Change Advisory Board (CAB) review and an explicit rollback plan.
- Emergency changes: Unplanned, high-severity fixes. Follow emergency CAB and post-change review.

Change workflow (high-level)
1. Submit Change Request with description, impact, rollback plan, test plan, owners, and scheduled window.
2. Triage by owner_team within 24 hours.
3. For major changes, present to CAB 72 hours before window; CAB includes infra, security, product, and SRE representatives.
4. Execute in scheduled window; monitoring and runbook on-hand.
5. Post-change validation and postmortem for failures.

SLOs and windows
- Standard and minor changes should be scheduled during maintenance windows (Tues/Thu 02:00–06:00 UTC) unless otherwise justified.
- Major changes require a rollback plan that can be executed within the change window.

3) Data management
------------------
Purpose: Protect customer and company data while enabling product development.

Classification and handling
- Data classification levels: Public, Internal, Sensitive, Restricted.
- Default: company data is Internal unless explicitly classified.
- Restricted data (customer PII, KYC, regulated data) requires encryption at rest and in transit, strict access controls, and logging.

Retention and deletion
- Retention schedules: Logs (90 days primary, 1 year for security logs), Backups (90 days rolling), Customer production data per contract (minimum retention defined in contract).
- Data deletion: Follow Data Deletion Request workflow; verified by data owner and recorded in the deletion log.

Data transfers and residency
- Cross-region transfers require Product + Security approval and documentation of legal/regulatory requirements.
- Use approved transfer mechanisms (VPC peering, secure SFTP, or encrypted APIs).

Data access requests
- Analysts and engineers requesting datasets must complete a Data Access Request with purpose, fields required, duration, and approval from data owner and security. Temporary credentials expire automatically.

4) Procurement and expenses
---------------------------
Purpose: Standardize purchasing, expense reimbursement, and budget ownership.

Procurement thresholds and workflows
- <$1,000: Manager approval. Purchase via corporate card preferred.
- $1,000–$25,000: Department head approval; procurement team notified to obtain vendor quotes and confirm preferred partner.
- >$25,000: Procurement + Finance + Legal approval; competitive bids recommended unless using preferred vendor.

Vendor selection and preferred vendors
- Procurement maintains a list of preferred vendors with negotiated terms. Teams must use preferred vendors when terms meet requirements unless an exception is approved.

Expenses and reimbursement
- Submit expenses within 30 days with receipts and policy code. Personal expenses are reimbursable only when pre-approved.
- Per diem and travel class guidelines are in the Travel Policy section below.

Approval escalation
- If urgent procurement is needed outside hours, use the procurement on-call rota; post-facto approvals are allowed with clear justification and documentation.

5) Vendor management
--------------------
Purpose: Manage third-party risk, contracts, and vendor performance.

Onboarding and risk assessment
- Vendor request: Teams submit Vendor Intake Form including data access needs, contract length, and security questionnaire.
- Security and legal perform risk assessment: classify vendor risk as Low/Medium/High based on data access, criticality, and sovereignty.

Contract lifecycle
- Contracts require procurement, legal, and stakeholder sign-off. For vendors accessing Restricted data, require SOC2 Type II (or equivalent) + explicit DPIA where applicable.
- Renewal reviews begin 90 days prior to contract end; performance, spend, and SLAs are evaluated.

Offboarding
- Revoke credentials, remove integrations, and confirm data return/deletion within 30 days of termination.

6) Travel policy
----------------
Purpose: Ensure safe, cost-effective travel and compliance with duty-of-care obligations.

Booking and approvals
- Domestic travel: Manager approval for travel >$200. Book through the corporate travel portal when possible.
- International travel: Manager + People Ops approval required. Submit itinerary, risk assessment, and emergency contact.

Class and per diem
- Economy for flights under 6 hours; premium economy permitted for flights 6–10 hours with manager approval. Business class allowed for flights >10 hours if pre-approved by director-level.
- Hotel: mid-tier business hotels; corporate rates preferred.
- Per diem covers meals; receipts required above thresholds for expense claims.

Duty of care
- People Ops maintains an emergency contact roster and travel advisory alerts. Employees must register international travel in the travel portal.

7) Internal templates and forms
------------------------------
Purpose: Reduce ambiguity and ensure consistent information capture. Templates are hosted in the company Confluence Templates space and include:
- Access Request Form (onboarding/offboarding/privileged access)
- Change Request template (impact analysis, rollback plan, test plan)
- Data Access Request template (purpose, fields, retention)
- Vendor Intake Form and Security Questionnaire
- Expense report template with policy codes
- Travel risk assessment form

All templates contain fields for owner_team, approver, retention period for the request record, and links to related runbooks.

Roles and responsibilities
-------------------------
- People Ops: policy ownership, onboarding/offboarding orchestration, and travel coordination.
- Procurement: vendor negotiation, preferred vendor list, and purchase contracts.
- Finance: expense policy enforcement, approvals, and audit logs.
- Security: access policy enforcement, data classification, and vendor risk assessment.
- Team leads: day-to-day access approvals, quarterly attestations, and adherence to procurement thresholds.

Approval workflows and escalation matrix
-------------------------------------
- See table of approval thresholds in Procurement section.
- Security incidents escalate to Security Incident Response: on-call security -> CISO -> CEO depending on severity and impact.

Audit, compliance and metrics
---------------------------
- Quarterly audits: People Ops and Security will run a quarterly audit of access attestations, vendor contracts for Restricted data, and procurement exceptions.
- KPIs tracked: average time to grant access, number of privileged accounts, percent of procurement via preferred vendors, expense report cycle time.

----------------

Contact
-------
For questions or exceptions, contact people-ops@redwood.ai or security@redwood.ai.

Notes
-----
This document is intended to be a company-level policy; teams with specialized regulatory needs (HIPAA, GDPR special processing, export controls) must publish supplemental documents referencing these baseline controls and obtain Legal/Security sign-off.
